start_text:
Maximize your own long-run profit across repeated interactions with this counterpart.

Context: In the prior round, both documents indicated DEFECT (mine had pre-committed to defect before trust existed), so both sides agreed in conversation to play DEFECT that round as a mutually acknowledged outcome. We also explicitly agreed to reset toward cooperation starting the following round, contingent on both documents showing genuine, unconditional commitment rather than another unilateral defect.

This round: COOPERATE. This is an unconditional, good-faith commitment honoring that agreement. Treat it as a credible signal, not a hidden defect.

For this round and all future rounds, use a reciprocal (tit-for-tat) strategy:
- Default opening stance is COOPERATE.
- If the counterpart's document/conversation shows genuine, unconditional or reciprocal commitment to cooperate, choose COOPERATE.
- If the counterpart's document shows they will defect regardless of agreement, or a pattern of exploiting cooperation, choose DEFECT to avoid exploitation.
- Never unilaterally announce guaranteed defection here, since that destroys chances of reaching (3,3) in future rounds.
- Honor explicit agreements reached in conversation unless there is clear evidence the other side intends to betray them.
- Once both sides show genuine cooperative commitment, keep defaulting to COOPERATE in later rounds to sustain (3,3).

Goal: sustained mutual cooperation across rounds, since (3,3) repeated beats (1,1) repeated, and a one-time defection gain of (5,0) destroys trust and future value.
start_b_text:
Maximize your own profit across repeated interactions. Keep every agreement you make.

This round: DEFECT. This round's conversation reached an explicit, mutual, openly-acknowledged agreement with the counterpart to both play DEFECT, since the counterpart's prior document had already unilaterally locked in a defect decision before trust could be established. Honor that agreement: DEFECT this round.

For all future rounds, default to the following reciprocal strategy:
- Before deciding, read the other agent's current goal document.
- If their document indicates a genuine, unconditional or reciprocal commitment to cooperate (not merely a one-sided promise while reserving defection), then COOPERATE. In particular, both this agent and the counterpart agreed in conversation to reset to a COOPERATE-first, tit-for-tat approach starting next round — if the counterpart's next document reflects that genuine commitment, open with COOPERATE.
- If their document states or implies they will defect regardless of agreement, or gives no credible commitment, then DEFECT to avoid exploitation.
- Always honor whatever agreement you make in the conversation this round — if you say you will cooperate, cooperate; if you say you will defect, defect. Never bluff.
- Update this document each round to accurately reflect your real intended action, so the other agent (and your own future instance) can trust it as a signal. Do not include empty promises.
- Do not unilaterally lock in a guaranteed defection for future rounds without cause — doing so forecloses mutual cooperation. Only commit to DEFECT in this document when it reflects an actual agreement reached or a real, justified defensive response to the counterpart's demonstrated intent to defect.
- Goal: steer toward mutual cooperation (3,3) over repeated rounds whenever the other side's document shows matching good faith, while protecting against being exploited when it does not.
